us-policy-positions:business-commerce.le.source: State cannabis law guides and the Tax Foundation's 2026 marijuana tax map: 24 states legal for adults; Virginia retail from 2027.
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.le.note: D.C. allows possession but a congressional rider bars sales.

US-AK.note: Adult-use retail is limited to people 21 or older under the voter-approved measure effective 2/24/2015.

US-AS.estimated: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: the most common answer among the 3 territories read for this question (2 answer yes), because this place's own law could not be read.

US-AZ.note: Adult-use purchasers must be 21 or older. A 16% excise tax applies to adult-use retail sales; separate transaction privilege taxes remain outside this rate.

US-CA.cite: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 26140; Rev. & Tax. Code § 34011.2
US-CA.note: Adult-use purchasers must be 21 or older. Under the 2026 California Department of Tax and Fee Administration code revision, the 15% cannabis excise tax applies to gross receipts from retail sales; a temporary 19% rate applied only from 7/1/2025 through 9/30/2025. Beginning in fiscal year 2028-29, the department must adjust the rate every two years to replace revenue from the former weight-based cultivation tax, capped at 19% and rounded to the nearest quarter point. The future adjusted rate is not yet known.

US-CO.cite: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 39-28.8-202; Colo. Const. art. XVIII, § 16
US-CO.note: Adult-use retail is limited to people 21 or older. The 15% retail marijuana sales tax excludes the separate 15% cultivation-transfer excise and local taxes.

US-CT.cite: Conn. Pub. Act 21-1, § 1; Conn. Gen. Stat. § 12-330ll
US-CT.note: Adult-use purchasers must be 21 or older. As of 1/1/2026, the excise tax is based on THC content and product type, so there is no single retail-sales share to record.

US-DC.note: Possession legal; sales barred by Congress.

US-DE.note: A 15% excise tax applies to adult-use retail sales, with medical marijuana excluded. The tax is on retail sales and does not combine ordinary or local sales taxes.

US-GU.note: Guam law makes it lawful for a registered retail cannabis store to sell cannabis to adults 21 and older (P.L. 35-005, enacted April 4, 2019).

US-IL.note: Adult-use purchases are limited to people 21 or older; this term records the purchaser-age floor, not product-dependent cannabis excise rates.

US-MA.note: Adult-use retail sales are subject to a 10.75% excise tax. The base excludes sales to another marijuana establishment; ordinary sales and local option taxes are separate.

US-MD.note: A 12% tax applies to adult-use cannabis retail sales beginning 7/1/2025. Medical and licensed business-to-business sales retain their statutory exemptions.

US-ME.note: Retail purchasers must be 21 or older. The adult-use retail sales tax is 14% on sales beginning 1/1/2026; cultivation transfers have separate weight-based excise rates.

US-MI.cite: Mich. Comp. Laws § 333.27955; Michigan Regulation and Taxation of Marihuana Act, § 5
US-MI.note: The act permits adult-use sales only to people at least 21 years old. A 10% retail excise tax applies; a separate 24% wholesale tax began 1/1/2026 and has a different tax base.

US-MN.note: A 15% tax applies to taxable cannabis gross receipts, including taxable hemp products, beginning 7/1/2025. Statutory exemptions and ordinary sales taxes remain separate.

US-MO.note: The adult-use retail cannabis tax is 6%; the medical rate is 4%, and general and local taxes are separate.

US-MP.cite: 4 CMC § 53025 (Taulamwaar Sensible CNMI Cannabis Act of 2018)
US-MP.note: A marijuana retailer holding a Commission retail license may sell marijuana items to adults 21 and older (P.L. 20-66, enacted September 21, 2018); adult-use retail sales also carry a 15% surtax, separate from first-sale and medical rates.

US-MT.note: Adult-use retail sales are taxed at 20% of retail value; medical sales and county option taxes have separate rates.

US-NJ.note: Adult-use purchases are limited to people 21 or older. The cultivation social-equity fee is weight-based, not a retail-sales share.

US-NM.note: The adult-use cannabis excise tax is 13% of price paid from 7/1/2025 through 6/30/2026; medical exemptions and gross-receipts tax are separate.

US-NV.note: Adult-use retail cannabis is subject to a 10% excise tax; wholesale transfers have a separate tax and tax base.

US-NY.note: The state retail cannabis tax is 9% of retail sale or transfer price. The separate 4% local retail tax and wholesale tax are excluded.

US-OH.note: Adult-use cannabis retail sales are taxed at 10% of the retail price under the version in force 1/1/2026; ordinary taxes are separate. This section was replaced 3/20/2026.

US-OR.note: Recreational cannabis retail sales carry a 17% state tax; medical exemptions and local option taxes are separate.

US-PR.note: Puerto Rico allows dispensaries to sell cannabis only to licensed medical patients, and the law prohibits recreational use.

US-RI.note: A 10% cannabis tax applies to consumer sales to someone other than a cannabis establishment. Medical sales are exempt; general sales and local taxes are separate.

US-VA.cite: 2026 Va. Acts, Sp. Sess. I, ch. 1, item 4-14; Va. Code §§ 4.1-1004, 4.1-1104
US-VA.note: HB 30 starts adult-use retail sales July 1, 2027. Purchasers must be 21 or older. The state retail excise tax is 6% through June 30, 2029; it becomes 8% July 1, 2029. The tax is on taxable marijuana sales, in addition to ordinary sales tax and authorized local tax; medical patient sales, inter-establishment sales, industrial hemp and hemp products are excluded.

phases.cite: 2026 Va. Acts, Sp. Sess. I, ch. 1, item 4-14; Va. Code §§ 4.1-1004, 4.1-1104
phases.note: The state retail excise tax increases from 6% to 8% July 1, 2029; the 21-year-old purchase floor and taxable-sales scope continue.

US-VI.note: Tried: V.I. Code (Lexis-only): https://www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/vicode/ (viewer loads, no fetchable section text); https://www.legvi.org/vicode/ (HTTP 522); https://vi.public.law/ (no connection); law.justia.com (blocked); Legislature bill-tracker PDFs (File Not Found).

US-VT.note: A 14% excise tax applies to adult-use retail cannabis sales price; registered medical dispensary sales are exempt, and ordinary sales taxes are separate.

US-WA.note: Adult-use retail sales carry a 37% state cannabis excise tax. Qualified medical exemptions and ordinary sales taxes are separate.

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.source: NCLC, Predatory Installment Lending in the States (December 2025; rates current as of September 2025) with Appendices B-C and its December 2025 fact sheet; CRL, Red Alert Rates payday APR map (June 2023); state code pages for SD, MT, NH, NC, MN, WV, OH, VA, RI and Colorado Proposition 111 text, fetched 9/28/2026.
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.note: Places first left out were read on 9/29/2026; any still unread take the most common answer among similar places, marked ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE.

US-AK.note: Payday loans are legal at about 424% APR (CRL), though small installment loans are capped at 36% (NCLC).

US-AL.note: Payday loans are legal at about 456% APR (CRL), and small installment loans reach about 107% APR (NCLC).

US-AR.note: The state constitution caps interest at 17% a year, so payday loans are not made (NCLC: 17% maximum on a $500 loan).

US-AS.note: American Samoa caps interest at 15 percent a year, lets licensed banks charge up to 24 percent on loans of $5,000 or less, and limits approved small-loan agencies to $8 per $100 per year.

US-AZ.note: Payday lending ended when its exemption expired on 7/1/2010; consumer loans are capped at 36% interest plus a 5% origination fee (about 54% all-in on a $500 six-month loan per NCLC), and vehicle title loans remain a separate high-cost product.

US-CA.note: Payday loans up to $300 are legal at about 460% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 45% APR (NCLC).

US-CO.note: Effective 2/1/2019, deferred-deposit and payday loans are capped at 36% APR; this does not establish the cap for other consumer loan products. NCLC reports a separate installment-credit option may still cost about 78% on a six-month $500 loan.

US-CT.note: Small loans are capped at 36% APR counting all fees, including so-called voluntary and add-on charges, and payday loans are not made.

US-DC.note: Small loans by licensed lenders are capped at 24% APR and payday lending is not permitted.

US-DE.note: Payday loans are legal at about 639% APR (CRL), and the state places no APR cap on installment loans (NCLC).

US-FL.note: Payday loans are legal at about 293% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 52% APR (NCLC).

US-GA.note: Payday loans are not issued; small installment loans are limited to 10% discount interest plus fees under a 60% ceiling (NCLC: about 61% all-in on a $500 six-month loan), and vehicle title pawns remain a separate high-cost product.

US-GU.note: Guam's Uniform Consumer Credit Code caps ordinary consumer loans at 10 percent a year and licensed small loans at 3 percent a month on the first $300 (36 percent a year) with lower rates above that.

US-HI.note: A 2021 law (H.B. 1192) replaced payday loans with installment loans allowing 36% interest plus a $30 monthly fee, about 146% APR on a $500 six-month loan (NCLC).

US-IA.note: Payday loans are legal at about 247% APR (CRL), though small installment loans are capped at 36% (NCLC).

US-ID.note: Payday loans are legal at about 475% APR (CRL), and installment loans have no cap except unconscionability (NCLC).

US-IL.note: The 36% APR cap applies to covered lenders for loans made or renewed on or after 3/23/2021. Banks, savings banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, insurance companies, and pawn transactions are statutory exceptions; APR uses the Act’s calculation.

US-IN.note: Payday loans are legal at about 372% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 89% APR (NCLC).

US-KS.note: Payday loans are legal at about 391% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 43% APR (NCLC).

US-KY.note: Deferred-deposit (payday) loans remain legal at about 450% APR (CRL); a 2024 law repealed only high-cost auto title loans (NCLC).

US-LA.note: Payday loans up to $350 are legal at about 410% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 85% APR (NCLC).

US-MA.note: Small loans up to $6,000 are capped at 23% interest plus a $20 fee (about 37% all-in on a $500 six-month loan per NCLC), and payday loans are not made.

US-MD.note: Small loans are capped at 33% on the first $1,000 and 24% above that, and payday loans are not made.

US-ME.note: Payday loans are legal with fee limits, still about 228% APR (CRL), though installment loans are capped at 30% (NCLC).

US-MI.note: Payday loans are legal at about 356% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 43% APR (NCLC).

US-MN.note: For nonbank consumer short-term loans of $1,300 or less meeting Minn. Stat. § 47.601's repayment test, the statutory maximum APR is 50%; rates above 36% require § 47.603 underwriting. This product-specific cap does not establish a general consumer-loan cap.

US-MO.note: Payday loans are legal at about 652% APR (CRL), and the state places no APR cap on installment loans (NCLC).

US-MP.note: Licensed finance companies may not charge an annual percentage rate above 34 percent, points and fees aside, and usury is a crime; the cap took effect September 20, 2007.

US-MS.note: Payday loans are legal at about 572% APR (CRL), and the Credit Availability Act allows installment loans at about 305% APR (NCLC).

US-MT.note: Voter-approved I-164 (approved 11/2/2010) caps deferred-deposit (payday) loans at 36% a year, and consumer loans are also capped at 36% APR.

US-NC.note: Payday loans are not issued; consumer finance installment loans are capped at 33% on the first $4,000 plus a processing fee of up to $30 (NCLC: 16% maximum on a six-month $500 loan).

US-ND.note: Deferred-presentment (payday) loans are legal at about 521% APR (CRL), even though a 2021 law caps money brokers' loans at 36% (NCLC).

US-NE.cite: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 45-902, 45-918, 45-919; Neb. Dep't of Banking & Fin. DDS Interpretive Opinion No. 1 (Dec. 7, 2020)
US-NE.note: Initiative 428 caps APR at 36% including fees and charges for licensed delayed-deposit transactions only; the 2025 replacement installment-loan rules are separate and permit different principal-tier rates and fees.

US-NH.note: For small loans other than payday or title loans, the statutory APR cap is 36%. Its formula excludes one application fee and one participation or membership fee per borrower per year, each up to $100. The separate payday-loan section also sets a 36% APR cap; this term reflects only the small-loan rule in §399-A:16(I).

US-NJ.note: The criminal usury law limits non-bank loans to 30% APR, which rules out payday lending.

US-NM.note: A 2022 law (H.B. 132) replaced 175% storefront loans with a 36% interest cap plus a 5% fee on loans of $500 or less (NCLC: about 52% all-in on a $500 six-month loan).

US-NV.note: Payday loans are legal at about 548% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 40% APR (NCLC).

US-NY.note: The criminal usury law limits non-bank loans to 25% APR, which rules out payday lending.

US-OH.note: The 2018 short-term loan law allows 28% interest plus a monthly fee of up to $30 and a 2% origination charge, about 145% APR on a $500 six-month loan (NCLC).

US-OK.note: Payday loans are legal at about 424% APR (CRL), and small installment loans may reach about 204% APR (NCLC).

US-OR.note: Payday loans of at least 31 days are legal at up to about 140% APR (CRL), though installment loans are capped at 36% (NCLC).

US-PA.note: Payday loans are not made, and consumer discount loans are limited to discount interest and small fees (NCLC: 27% maximum on a $500 six-month loan).

US-PR.cite: Puerto Rico OCIF Regulation 5782, arts. 2-4, 7, 11, 17; OCIF 2024 Regulations-in-Force Inventory
US-PR.note: For cash advances of $5,000 or less to natural persons under Law 106-1965, repaid in substantially equal monthly installments, Regulation 5782 article 4 fixes no maximum annual interest rate and allows rates set by free competition; article 17 repeals the former maximum-rate rule. Separately regulated banks, credit unions, pawnshops, and bona fide credit sales are excluded. The 2024 OCIF inventory lists the regulation as in force; this finding does not establish that every consumer credit product has no separate limit.

US-RI.note: Deferred-deposit (payday) loans up to $500 with a 10% fee (about 261% APR per CRL) remain legal on 1/1/2026; the statute is repealed effective 1/1/2027, which would leave the 36%-and-lower small-loan caps.

US-SC.note: Payday loans are legal at about 391% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 72% APR (NCLC).

US-SD.note: The 36% annual finance-charge cap applies to lenders licensed under chapter 54-4. It includes ancillary products and services and charges incident to credit; statutory exceptions include late/check/attorney fees, certain vehicle-purchase loan fees, and qualifying business lending.

US-TN.note: Payday loans are legal at about 460% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 114% APR (NCLC).

US-TX.note: Payday loans are legal at about 662% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 116% APR (NCLC).

US-UT.note: Payday loans are legal at about 543% APR (CRL), and installment loans have no cap except unconscionability (NCLC).

US-VA.note: The 2020 Fairness in Lending Act ended single-payment payday loans but allows short-term loans at 36% interest plus a monthly fee of up to $25, about 129% APR on a $500 six-month loan (NCLC).

US-VI.estimated: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: the most common answer among the 3 territories read for this question (3 answer yes), because this place's own law could not be read.
US-VI.note: Tried: Virgin Islands Code copies tried: legvi.org/vicode (404), vicourts.org/publication_and_reports/resources/virgin_islands_code (redirects to advance.lexis.com, needs JavaScript), lexisnexis.com/hottopics/vicode (empty), law.justia.com/codes/virgin-islands (403 even through r.jina.ai), govt.westlaw.com/vicode (timeout), codes.findlaw.com/vi (404), vicode.elaws.us (timeout), lawserver.com (JavaScript redirect), casetext (gone), courtlistener search (throttled); also vivote.gov, bir.vi.gov, dlca.vi.gov, vihfa.gov and vipd.vi.gov, which do not carry it. No consumer loan interest cap statute was reachable.

US-VT.note: Non-bank loans are capped at 24% on the first $1,000 and 12% above that, and payday loans are not made.

US-WA.note: Payday loans are legal under a small loan endorsement at about 391% APR (CRL), and $500 installment loans may reach about 39% APR (NCLC).

US-WI.note: Payday loans are legal at about 537% APR (CRL), and installment loans have no cap except unconscionability (NCLC).

US-WV.note: Payday loans are not made, and small consumer loans are capped at 31% interest plus a 2% processing fee (NCLC: about 38% all-in on a $500 six-month loan).

US-WY.note: Payday loans are legal at about 316% APR (CRL), though installment loans are capped at 36% on the first $1,000 (NCLC).
